title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: From high-tech engineering hubs to quiet library floors and scenic rooftop terraces, Auburn offers a diverse range of environments for focused academic work.

cards.title: Quiet Zone on the Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: RBD Library Quiet Study
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor for a strictly enforced quiet environment. It is the go-to spot for deep focus and individual work away from the collaborative buzz of the lower levels.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet study floor in the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth floor of the Ralph Brown Draughon Library is designated as an individual quiet study area.
cards.source_title: Are there any quiet study areas in the library? - LibAnswers
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; check library hours for late-night access during finals.

cards.title: Glass-Enclosed Group Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mell Classroom Building @ RBD
cards.notes: Reserve one of the 40 glass-enclosed study rooms via the online booking system. These spaces offer acoustic privacy and integrated technology for group projects.
cards.short_summary: Modern, reservable group study rooms with high-tech amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mell Classroom Building features 40 study rooms that can be reserved using the Skedda system.
cards.source_title: Mell Classroom Building | EASL - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via aub.ie/studyroombooking; check-in within 10 minutes.

cards.title: Gavin Terrace Rooftop
cards.subtitle: Harbert College of Business
cards.notes: Study with a view of Jordan-Hare Stadium from this fourth-floor rooftop terrace. It features covered seating and power outlets for outdoor productivity.
cards.short_summary: A scenic rooftop terrace offering outdoor study space for business students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gavin Terrace on the fourth floor of Horton-Hardgrave Hall offers collaborative working spaces and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

cards.title: Engineering Achievement Hub
cards.subtitle: Brown-Kopel Center
cards.notes: Utilize the spacious study areas on the top floor or the ground-floor maker spaces. This center is designed for collaboration across all engineering disciplines.
cards.short_summary: A comprehensive active-learning environment for engineering students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brown-Kopel Center includes ample student study areas, maker spaces, and laboratories across three stories.
cards.source_title: Brown-Kopel Engineering Student Achievement Center - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Check current semester hours for building access.

cards.entity_name: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
cards.title: Artistic Inspiration in the Lobby
cards.subtitle: Museum Study Space
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner among modular couches in the museum lobby. It is a peaceful alternative to the library, with free admission and an on-site café.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, art-filled study environment with modular seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lobby has modular couches for group sessions or relaxed reading, and admission is free.
cards.source_title: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art - College Students
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; extended hours until 8 p.m. on Thursdays.

cards.title: ACLC Relaxation Zones
cards.subtitle: Academic Classroom Complex
cards.notes: Located next to The Edge dining hall, this complex features adaptable classrooms and dedicated quiet study areas for students between labs.
cards.short_summary: Modern quiet study and relaxation areas within a major lab complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The ACLC features adaptable classroom spaces, labs, and quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Auburn University opens new Academic Classroom and Laboratory Complex
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic building hours.

cards.title: Student Center Quiet Lounges
cards.subtitle: Melton Student Center
cards.notes: The third floor offers quiet study areas and meeting spaces. It is a central campus hub with easy access to dining and student resources.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study lounges located on the upper floor of the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harold D. Melton Student Center offers meeting spaces and quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Harold D. Melton Student Center - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check for specific holiday or break hours.

cards.entity_name: Tony and Libba Rane Culinary Science Center
cards.title: Woltosz Rooftop Terrace
cards.subtitle: Rane Culinary Science Center
cards.notes: Visit this rooftop garden before 3 p.m. for a quiet study session with views of Samford Hall. It features sun-soaked seating and shaded umbrellas.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop garden terrace open to students during daytime hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walt and Ginger Woltosz Rooftop Terrace is open to students until 3 p.m. each day.
cards.source_title: Find out where students are studying this fall - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Student access ends at 3 p.m. daily before transitioning to a commercial venue.

cards.title: Lowder Ground Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: Harbert College of Business
cards.notes: Located near the Starbucks on the ground floor, this area (Room 023) provides a convenient spot for business students to work between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated student study area on the ground floor of the business building.
cards.evidence_claim: Lowder Hall Ground Floor features a student study area in room 023.
cards.source_title: Harbert College of Business Locations - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Primarily for students enrolled in Harbert College of Business classes.

cards.title: FWE Student Organization Lounge
cards.subtitle: College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment
cards.notes: The second floor houses a student lounge and organization space (Room 2207). It offers a quiet, specialized environment for natural resource majors.
cards.short_summary: A specialized student lounge and study area for FWE majors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forestry and Wildlife Sciences Building includes a student organization and lounge area on the second floor.
cards.source_title: FWE Building Room Directory - College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment
cards.access_notes: Access may be restricted to students within the College of Forestry, Wildlife and Environment.
